deals.evidence: Nashville Soccer Holdings LLC has acquired a majority interest in DMD Soccer
deals.headline: John Ingram's Nashville Soccer Holdings takes majority control of Nashville SC owner DMD Soccer
deals.investor: Nashville Soccer Holdings LLC (John R. Ingram)
deals.summary: Ingram's MLS-bid vehicle acquired a majority interest in DMD Soccer, which had won the USL franchise in 2016 under David Dill, Marcus Whitney and Chris Redhage, uniting the USL club with the MLS bid. Price and percentage were not disclosed.

deals.evidence: separately is tasked with covering a $150 million expansion fee with MLS
deals.headline: Ingram group awarded MLS expansion club, owes $150m fee
deals.investor: Nashville Soccer Holdings, LLC (John Ingram, the Wilf family and the Turner family)
deals.summary: MLS awarded Nashville its 24th franchise on 20 December 2017; NBC Sports, reporting the 2018 stadium approval, said the ownership group was separately responsible for the $150m expansion fee.

deals.evidence: floated $225 million worth of bonds in late 2019 to fund construction of a soccer-specific stadium
deals.headline: Metro Sports Authority floats $225m of bonds to build GEODIS Park; Nashville SC to repay
deals.investor: Revenue bondholders (bonds issued by the Metro Nashville Sports Authority)
deals.summary: The Sports Authority, which owns all of Nashville's sports venues, leased the Fairgrounds land for 30 years, floated $225m of bonds in late 2019 to fund the stadium and leased it to Nashville SC for 30 years; the club has near-total control of the building and will pay off the bonds. Metro puts the stadium's cost at $335m.

founded_evidence: Nashville SC was awarded a USL franchise in July 2016 to the DMD Soccer group
name: Nashville Soccer Club
notes: Replaces the earlier record's Wikipedia capacity (30,000) with Metro's 30,109. Forbes is cited through the Internet Archive snapshot of its February 2026 MLS list because forbes.com article pages refuse automated fetches, and Nashville has no forbes.com/teams page (not on Forbes' May 2026 world soccer list). Revenue and operating income (EBITDA) are Forbes estimates for the 2025 season. Sportico's February 2026 dataset values the club at $670m with $70m revenue. Founded year is the July 2016 USL franchise award to DMD Soccer; the MLS franchise followed on 20 December 2017 and MLS play began in 2020. In 2018 the stadium plan had Metro issuing $225m of revenue bonds and the team contributing $25m up front, covering overruns and paying about $9m a year under a 30-year lease (NBC Sports); SBJ (2022) reports the club repays the bonds. Vice chairman Ian Ayre's remit since January 2025 includes 'team investments and fundraising/capital raises', but no stake sale since 2022 was found. The Wilf family deal records only their exit; the buyer is not stated. No CEO title exists at present: Lindsey Paola (Chief Business Officer) runs day-to-day business and reports to chairman John Ingram. Not found on a citable page: stake percentages for any owner, the registry number of Nashville Soccer Holdings, LLC, average attendance, and social-media follower counts.

ownership_summary: Nashville SC is majority-owned by John R. Ingram, chairman of Ingram Industries, through Nashville Soccer Holdings, LLC, which took a majority interest in founding owner DMD Soccer in May 2017. His partners include the Turner family (MarketStreet Enterprises) and, since April 2022, minority owners Reese Witherspoon, Jim Toth and Derrick Henry. The Wilf family (Minnesota Vikings) were partners at the 2017 MLS award but dissolved their minority stake in 2021 when they bought Orlando City. No stake percentages are published, and no fund or institutional investor is reported.
